briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. Welcome. We will now begin the climate change expert spokesperson briefing for August 8, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Unprecedented Extreme Weather Events and Severe Damages
sections.content: Recently, unprecedented extreme weather events have led to a surge in damages both domestically and internationally. In South Korea, continuous heatwaves have caused a sharp increase in heat-related illnesses and even fatalities [14, 19]. The heat has also severely impacted society as a whole, leading to water supply disruptions due to burst water pipes and the suspension of driver's license tests [6, 13, 17, 20, 24]. Furthermore, the East Coast experienced torrential rainfall of 80mm per hour, resulting in road flooding [15], and regions simultaneously facing heatwaves and drought have declared emergencies regarding water supply [6, 16]. Internationally, deadly wildfires have persisted in areas such as Canada, France, Greece, and Scotland, causing deteriorating air quality and resident evacuations [41, 42, 43, 44]. Extreme heatwaves across Europe and various regions worldwide are also leading to casualties and economic losses [32, 43].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Climate Crisis Response Policy Discussions and National Capacity Building
sections.content: As the climate crisis intensifies, national-level responses and policy discussions are actively underway both domestically and internationally. The Haenam County Mayor emphasized the urgency of a 'national control tower' to devise solutions for the climate crisis [4], and key concepts such as assessing greenhouse gas risks are being discussed [5]. Meanwhile, concepts like 'Project Hail Mary,' which involves blocking the sun as a 'last resort' to combat heatwaves, are being discussed, reflecting the sense of crisis [1]. Domestically, Uljin County is holding an interim evaluation meeting for climate change-resilient food crops, demonstrating practical adaptation efforts at the local level [2]. Korea University is also planning to host a Model UN Climate Change Conference to foster future climate leaders [3].

sections.title: 🌱 Accelerating Renewable Energy Transition and Corporate Contributions
sections.content: Efforts to transition to renewable energy, a crucial solution for overcoming the climate crisis, are accelerating both domestically and internationally. Hanjaeyeon and the Korea Energy Agency are strengthening policy and technological cooperation by holding working-level consultations for a major renewable energy transition [7]. Active participation from corporations continues, with HD Hyundai Construction Equipment, for example, increasing its share of renewable energy to achieve 'RE100' [9]. In the solar power sector, large-scale projects are becoming visible, including the groundbreaking of the Haenam solar power plant after overcoming 10 years of regulations [10], the signing of an MOU for a solar project utilizing bicycle paths [11], and the launch of the nation's largest single-site solar project, comparable in scale to a thermal power plant [12]. However, the solar industry is pointing out arbitrary interpretations of BIPV (Building-Integrated Photovoltaics) certification standards and urging institutional improvements [8], indicating a greater need for policy support and clarity.

sections.title: ⚠️ Widespread Impacts of Climate Change: Ecosystems, Agriculture, and Daily Life
sections.content: Climate change extends beyond mere weather anomalies, exerting broad and profound impacts across ecosystems, agriculture, and our daily lives. Wine producers across Europe are facing challenges due to climate change [27, 39], and rice farmers in the Philippines are on the front lines of the battle against climate change, raising concerns about food security [28]. Furthermore, ecological changes are being detected, such as increased humidity in Connecticut and familiar jungle babblers being under pressure [29, 38]. Domestically, growing interest in how animals cope with summer heatwaves [23] and methods for consuming vegetables during summer [21] demonstrates that climate change is also affecting our food culture and animal welfare.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has once again highlighted the unprecedented crisis brought about by climate change and the multifaceted efforts required to address it. International cooperation and the swift implementation of domestic policies will become even more crucial for a sustainable future. This concludes the climate briefing for August 8, 2026.
